text.p: Hasbro Inc. Monday said its earnings rose about 11 percent in the third quarter, in line with expectations on Wall Street, boosted by strong sales of Batman and Star Wars action figures and some of its new games.

The company, one of the nation's largest toy makers said net profit rose to $70.5 million in the quarter from $63.6 million in the 1995 period. Earnings per share rose to 81 cents from 72 cents. Sales grew 2 percent to $845.1 million from $826.2 million.

Strong sales of boys' toys, including the Batman and Star Wars figures, Milton Bradley and Parker Brothers games, and the leading seller, the Baby Go Bye Bye large doll, paced results, Pawtucket, R.I.-based Hasbro said.
New items that performed well included the Puzz 3D puzzle and the game Goosebumps.
Hasbro stock fell 37.5 cents to $38.75 on the American Stock Exchange. Analysts had expected earnings of 80 cents a share on average, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
